Model a cantilever beam of length L = 1800 mm, fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L, using Euler–Bernoulli beam theory (small deflection, linear elastic).
Use the N–mm–MPa unit system throughout (E in N/mm², I in mm⁴, P in N, L in mm).
Material: structural steel with Young's modulus E = 200000 MPa (i.e., 200000 N/mm²).
Cross-section: constant second moment of area I = 1200000 mm⁴.
Loading: a single downward point load P = 2000 N applied at the free end (x = L).
No external couple is applied at the free end.
The bending moment diagram is linear: M(x) = P(L − x), equal to PL at the fixed end and zero at the free end.
Compute the free-end slope using θ(L) = PL² / (2EI) and report it in radians and in degrees.
Compute the free-end vertical deflection using δ(L) = PL³ / (3EI) and report it in mm.
All intermediate quantities must carry consistent N–mm–MPa units so that the final slope is dimensionless (radians) and the final deflection is in mm.
